        Moving to a new machinePack everything into one file, and unpack it on the new one.
        
On the old machine, Move out takes a fresh backup, stops every app, and packs the settings, the apps' data, and the newest database dumps into one file. On the new one, install Homelab Wizard, choose Set it up for me, plug in the drive with the photos and media, and Move in with that file: the databases load and the apps that ran before start again.

        
 

      

      

        How the backups workNightly copies, encrypted off-site, and a monthly restore test.
        
Every night at 03:30 the homelab copies each app's database, a few volumes, and its settings file into recovery-staging. From 05:00 Duplicati encrypts those copies and the apps' folders into the backup destination. A copy older than a day and a bit is marked stale, and the watchdog sends an alert; a copy whose app waits for its drive to be plugged in is paused instead, and its last copies are kept.

      
Prove a restore once a month: click Test a restore. Duplicati restores a dozen files from last night's Homelab AppData backup into recovery-staging/restore-test, each is compared with the live file, and the restore is removed when they match. The result shows here, and the nightly job reminds you when it is over 30 days old. A full restore is in Disaster Recovery.
